# UX Requirements Quality Checklist: Gestor musical

**Purpose**: Review whether the feature specification clearly defines the music-manager experience, scope boundaries, and user-focused UX requirements without ambiguity.
**Created**: 2026-08-14
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

## Requirement Completeness

- [ ] CHK001 Are the exact primary views and navigation paths for home, songs, artists, albums, playlists, and favorites explicitly defined across the feature? [Completeness, Spec §User Story 1-5]
- [ ] CHK002 Are all core music-manager tasks represented in requirements, including browsing catalog, viewing details, playlist access, and favorites management? [Completeness, Spec §FR-001 to FR-015]
- [ ] CHK003 Are the mandatory exclusions documented clearly enough to prevent scope drift into backend, social, or streaming features? [Completeness, Spec §Input and FR-009 to FR-015]
- [ ] CHK004 Are the key user journeys mapped to primary and secondary priorities so the MVP boundary is clear? [Completeness, Spec §User Story 1-5]

## Requirement Clarity

- [ ] CHK005 Is the meaning of "login or access entry screen" specific enough to clarify whether it is a simulated entry flow or a real authentication experience? [Clarity, Spec §FR-001]
- [ ] CHK006 Is "resumen del contenido disponible" defined with enough specificity for what the home screen must surface? [Clarity, Spec §User Story 1]
- [ ] CHK007 Are the criteria for identifying songs, artists, albums, and playlists clear enough to avoid ambiguous catalog labeling? [Clarity, Spec §FR-003 to FR-007]
- [ ] CHK008 Is the distinction between list and detail views defined precisely enough to prevent confusion in navigation and information hierarchy? [Clarity, Spec §FR-011]
- [ ] CHK009 Is the term "favoritos" defined in a way that clarifies which item types can be saved, removed, and revisited? [Clarity, Spec §FR-008 and §FR-014]

## Requirement Consistency

- [ ] CHK010 Are the user journeys consistent with the explicit product boundary of a local simulated experience rather than a backend-driven platform? [Consistency, Spec §Input and §FR-009]
- [ ] CHK011 Do the navigation and detail-view requirements align across the song, artist, album, playlist, and favorites flows? [Consistency, Spec §FR-011 and §User Story 2-5]
- [ ] CHK012 Are the descriptions of local mock data and the exclusions of real services consistent with every requirement? [Consistency, Spec §FR-009 and §Assumptions]
- [ ] CHK013 Are the language and scope assumptions in Spanish consistent with the product requirement to present the experience in Spanish? [Consistency, Spec §FR-010]

## Acceptance Criteria Quality

- [ ] CHK014 Are the success criteria measurable enough to be objectively validated without implementation details? [Acceptance Criteria, Spec §Success Criteria]
- [ ] CHK015 Can the primary navigation success metric be evaluated without depending on a specific technology stack or framework choice? [Acceptance Criteria, Spec §SC-001 to SC-006]
- [ ] CHK016 Are the measurable outcomes aligned with the actual user goals of discovery, catalog browsing, and favorites retention? [Acceptance Criteria, Spec §SC-001 to SC-006]
- [ ] CHK017 Are the acceptance scenarios written as clear user outcomes rather than implementation steps? [Acceptance Criteria, Spec §User Story 1-5]

## Scenario Coverage

- [ ] CHK018 Are primary scenarios covered for entry into the app, browsing the catalog, opening details, and revisiting favorites? [Coverage, Spec §User Story 1-5]
- [ ] CHK019 Are alternate navigation paths defined for returning from detail screens to the list context? [Coverage, Spec §Edge Cases]
- [ ] CHK020 Are exception flows documented for missing or invalid catalog items, empty collections, and incomplete records? [Coverage, Spec §Edge Cases and §FR-013]
- [ ] CHK021 Are recovery or fallback behaviors defined for item removal, empty favorites, and unresolved navigation states? [Coverage, Spec §Edge Cases]

## Edge Case Coverage

- [ ] CHK022 Are requirements defined for missing song, artist, album, or playlist records in the local catalog? [Edge Case, Gap, Spec §Edge Cases]
- [ ] CHK023 Are requirements defined for toggling favorites on and off without state ambiguity? [Edge Case, Spec §Edge Cases]
- [ ] CHK024 Are empty-state requirements defined for playlists that contain no songs and favorites that contain no saved items? [Edge Case, Spec §FR-013 and §Edge Cases]
- [ ] CHK025 Are requirements defined for back-navigation from detail screens so the user can return to the correct list context? [Edge Case, Spec §Edge Cases]

## Non-Functional Requirements

- [ ] CHK026 Are accessibility requirements defined beyond general product language, especially for touch targets, readability, and navigation clarity? [Non-Functional, Spec §Assumptions and Constitution]
- [ ] CHK027 Are responsiveness or multi-screen layout requirements defined for the mobile experience in a measurable and implementation-agnostic way? [Non-Functional, Spec §Assumptions]
- [ ] CHK028 Are performance expectations defined for local catalog browsing and quick navigation without external services? [Non-Functional, Spec §SC-001 to SC-006]
- [ ] CHK029 Are localization requirements clearly specified for Spanish-first interface labels and content, including any intentional exceptions? [Non-Functional, Spec §FR-010]

## Dependencies & Assumptions

- [ ] CHK030 Are the assumptions about single-user local behavior and the absence of real registration explicitly stated and consistent with the feature boundaries? [Assumption, Spec §Assumptions]
- [ ] CHK031 Are the dependencies on local mock content clearly documented as the only source of truth for the music catalog? [Dependency, Spec §FR-009 and §Assumptions]
- [ ] CHK032 Are the assumptions about non-social product scope and non-collaborative flows clearly bounded to avoid accidental feature expansion? [Assumption, Spec §Input and §Assumptions]
- [ ] CHK033 Is there a clear statement that the product is a simulated music manager rather than a streaming platform or service aggregator? [Clarity, Spec §Input]

## Ambiguities & Conflicts

- [ ] CHK034 Is the requirement for a "login or access entry screen" free of ambiguity about whether it is a decorative splash screen, a simulated login, or an access gate? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-001]
- [ ] CHK035 Are any terms such as "resumen", "destacadas", or "ruta de navegación comprensible" defined in objective terms that a reviewer can validate? [Ambiguity, Spec §User Story 1]
- [ ] CHK036 Are there any hidden or conflicting requirements between local simulation and the implied user expectations of a richer music app? [Conflict, Spec §Input and §FR-009 to FR-015]
- [ ] CHK037 Is the requirement for playlists explicit about whether they are user-created, curated, or fixed seeded content? [Gap, Spec §FR-007 and §Key Entities]

## Notes

- Mark items `[x]` only after review confirms the requirement-quality criterion is satisfied.
- Leave items unchecked when they still require clarification, correction, or reviewer evaluation.
- `/speckit-implement` reads checklist state as a gate and must not modify markers.
- `checklists/requirements.md` has a separate built-in lifecycle maintained by `/speckit-specify` and `/speckit-clarify`.
- The checklist focuses on requirements quality, not on implementation correctness or runtime behavior.
- It reflects the feature-specific constraints of a no-backend, local-data music manager experience.
